thread:
sanjay: Heads up — we just saw a ~3x 95th latency spike on runtime-prod around 11:12 UTC, lots of tail latency for short requests. Dashboards show throughput drop but host-level CPU/GPU utilisation looks normal. No obvious deploy in that window. 

eva: :eyes: linking dashboard — https://dash.redwood/internal/runtime/latency?range=1h (screenshot in thread). Is this across all models?

sanjay: looks concentrated on model-family: lm-small and lm-medium. lm-large unaffected. Also KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% for a subset of pods.

lina: any traces for slow requests? I’m not seeing traces for many of the affected request ids — seems sampled out.

sanjay: yeah that's the weird part — our trace sampling shows rate 1% but traces are missing for that cohort. last trace ingestion for that shard was 11:10 then a DSN error for ~5m.

perf-bot: profiling job finished: profile://176880-pprof.tar.gz — heap allocations spike on host gpu-09 at 11:11. Top symbol: runtime::kv_cache::lookup + 38%.

marcus: deploy-bot shows a config push at 10:58 but it was to routing rules (no model binary). No canary.

eva: Could this be noisy-neighbor eviction in KV cache causing extra kernel selection churn? If cache miss -> longer prefix -> different kernel chosen -> spike.

lina: I grabbed a p99 request trace from app logs (no full trace):
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:33Z] req=abcd123 host=gpu-09 model=lm-small seq=64 kv_hit=false kernel=matmul_fused_v2 latency_ms=318
[2026-03-15T11:12:33Z] req=abcd123 step=compile kernel_select=matmul_fused_v2 compile_ms=24
```

sanjay: Also noticed log sampling config was recently lowered from 10% -> 1% for cost reasons last week. That explains missing traces. Ops: can we temporarily bump sampling for runtime-prod until we finish triage?

ops-bot: request noted. Increasing trace/log sampling to 10% for runtime-prod (shard: all) — will revert in 2h.

eva: I pulled kernel selection histogram: before window most lm-small requests used matmul_fused_v1, during spike >60% switched to matmul_fused_v2 which is slower for short sequences. Change correlated with KV miss increase.

marcus: any config or auto-tuner that could flip kernel choice? We shipped a small compiler tweak last month that alters threshold for v2 when seq_len<128. Could be that.

perf-bot: quick diff of builds: compiler-rewrite#b7c -> changes matmul_fused fallback threshold from 48->32 in runtime kernel selector. That would cause narrower ranges for v1 and push more requests to v2 when caching behavior changes.

eva: ah — so KV miss increases -> longer prefixes -> runtime sees different token distribution -> kernel selector picks v2 more often. Nice chain.

sanjay: mitigation plan: 1) revert threshold change on canary hosts, 2) increase KV cache capacity on hotspot shard, 3) restore trace sampling to 100% for 10m to capture full traces, 4) add an alert for kernel-selection-ratio drift. Who owns 1)?

marcus: I can revert threshold on 2 canaries now. Pushing patch -> deploy started.

deploy-bot: deploy started by marcus: rollout id d9f3, targets: runtime-canary-{a,b}.

lina: with sampling up to 10% we got full traces for 15 slow requests — they show cache eviction during parallel warmups, followed by kernel compile path on hot host.

perf-bot: after canary revert, p95 for lm-small on canary nodes decreased from 280ms -> 120ms. Non-canary still elevated.

sanjay: rolling revert to production pinned to 4 hosts, will push in 15m if canary looks stable. Also we need long-term fix: adapt kernel selector to consider cache-hit signals (prefer v1 if cache miss spike detected) + increase default cache size for small models.

eva: created a follow-up ticket: https://issues.redwood/RT-2248 "kernel selector drift + kv cache feedback loop". Added owners and next steps.

ops-bot: trace sampling reverted to original 1% at request of costs; leave it at 10% until 13:30 UTC per request.

marcus: prod revert completed. Post-revert telemetry shows p95 back near baseline. I'll run regression tests tomorrow to ensure no other models impacted.

sanjay: big thanks. Observability gaps: we need durable trace ingestion and a dashboard showing trace-coverage by shard so next time we don't get blind spots.

lina: agree — also add a logging-level/retention playbook for incident responders (where to bump sampling, how to collect kernel-selection histograms quickly).

eva: I'll add a dashboard panel for kernel-selection ratio and KV hit rate with alert thresholds.

sanjay: closing thread once RT-2248 is in triage and canary metrics are green for 1h. :thumbsup:
